question: Which Wisconsin statute specifically governs a licensee's use of approved forms and the provision of legal advice in a real estate transaction?
choice_a: Wis. Stat. § 452.40
choice_b: Wis. Stat. § 452.135
choice_c: Wis. Stat. § 452.14
choice_d: Wis. Stat. § 452.03
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.40, titled "Use of forms; provision of legal advice," authorizes firms and licensees to use board-approved forms and restricts licensees from giving legal advice or opinions about the legal rights or obligations of parties to a transaction.
source_note: Wis. Stat. § 452.40 (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1e), what is an "approved form"?
choice_a: A contractual or conveyance form that is either prepared and approved by the Real Estate Examining Board under § 452.05(1)(b), Stats., or approved under § REEB 16.03
choice_b: Any purchase contract that a majority of licensees in the county customarily use
choice_c: A form drafted by any Wisconsin-licensed attorney regardless of board approval
choice_d: A form that has been recorded with the county register of deeds
explanation: REEB 16.02(1e) defines "approved form" as a contractual or conveyance form prepared and approved by the board under § 452.05(1)(b), Stats., or approved in § REEB 16.03. Attorney drafting or common local usage does not, by itself, make a form an "approved form."
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1e) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(5), what does it mean for a licensee to "use a form"?
choice_a: To complete a contractual or conveyance form by filling in blanks or modifying its printed provisions to carry out a party's instructions in a specific real estate transaction
choice_b: To physically print or photocopy a blank form for office inventory
choice_c: To notarize a form once all parties have signed it
choice_d: To advertise that a particular form is available from the firm
explanation: REEB 16.02(5) defines "use a form" as completing a contractual or conveyance form by filling in blanks or modifying printed provisions for the purpose of accomplishing a party's instruction in a specific transaction — this is the act the rest of Chapter REEB 16 regulates.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(5) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(2) and (3), what is the key difference between an "exclusive right to sell listing" and an "exclusive agency listing"?
choice_a: In an exclusive right to sell listing the firm earns a commission no matter who sells the property, including the owner, while an exclusive agency listing lets the owner sell the property without owing the listing firm a commission
choice_b: An exclusive agency listing can be given to multiple firms at once, while an exclusive right to sell listing can only ever be given to one firm
choice_c: An exclusive right to sell listing has no expiration date, while an exclusive agency listing must expire within 30 days
choice_d: There is no substantive difference; the two terms are interchangeable under REEB 16
explanation: REEB 16.02(3) defines an exclusive right to sell listing as entitling the firm to a commission if the property sells during the term regardless of who procures the buyer, including the owner. REEB 16.02(2) defines an exclusive agency listing as containing all the same elements except that the owner retains the right to sell without owing a commission.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(2), (3) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(4), how is an "open listing" defined?
choice_a: A written listing agreement that may be given to any number of firms, with the first firm to secure a buyer under its terms earning the commission
choice_b: A listing agreement that must be posted publicly on the firm's website
choice_c: A listing agreement that automatically converts to an exclusive right to sell listing after 90 days
choice_d: A listing agreement that can only be used for commercial property, not residential property
explanation: REEB 16.02(4) defines an open listing as a written listing agreement that the owner may give to any number of firms simultaneously, with whichever firm first secures a buyer under the listing's terms earning the commission.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(4) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(4m), a "one-party listing" differs from an exclusive right to sell listing in what way?
choice_a: The listing firm is entitled to a commission only if the property is sold to a specific party or parties identified in the written listing contract, rather than to any buyer
choice_b: A one-party listing can only be signed by a single licensee at the firm, never by a team
choice_c: A one-party listing waives the firm's right to any commission whatsoever
choice_d: A one-party listing may only be used when the property has a single co-owner
explanation: REEB 16.02(4m) defines a one-party listing as containing all the elements of an exclusive right to sell listing except that the firm earns a commission only if the property is sold to a specific party or parties named in the contract.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(4m) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(a), the board recognizes as approved which category of forms for deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, and land contracts?
choice_a: Forms prepared and approved by the State Bar of Wisconsin
choice_b: Forms prepared by any title insurance company doing business in Wisconsin
choice_c: Forms drafted by the buyer's or seller's individual attorney for that specific transaction
choice_d: Forms published by the National Association of REALTORS®
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(a) approves forms prepared and approved by the State Bar of Wisconsin for deeds, mortgages, mortgage notes, truth-in-lending disclosures, land contracts, release of mortgage, satisfaction of mortgage, assignment of mortgage, and assignment of land contract.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(a) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(c), when may a licensee use a contractual form for property located in another state?
choice_a: When the form is one that licensees may legally and customarily use for such a transaction in the state where the property is located
choice_b: Only if the Wisconsin board has independently reviewed and stamped that specific out-of-state form
choice_c: Never — Wisconsin licensees may only use forms approved for Wisconsin property
choice_d: Only if the out-of-state form is first translated into a Wisconsin State Bar template
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(c) approves contractual forms for the sale, purchase, or rental of real estate or a business opportunity located in another state, provided those are forms licensees may legally and customarily use for such transactions in the state where the property is located.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(c) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(e), who may prepare an approved property management agreement between a firm and a landlord?
choice_a: The broker entering into the agreement, an attorney, or the landlord
choice_b: Only the Real Estate Examining Board itself may draft property management agreements
choice_c: Only a tenant's attorney may draft the agreement
choice_d: Only the State Bar of Wisconsin may draft the agreement
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(e) approves property management agreement forms containing leasing, managing, marketing, and overall property management provisions when prepared by the broker entering into the agreement, an attorney, or the landlord.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(e) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: As a general rule under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(1), when must a licensee use board-approved forms?
choice_a: Whenever the licensee is acting as an agent or as a party in a real estate or business opportunity transaction, except as otherwise permitted under REEB 16.04(2) and (3)
choice_b: Only when the transaction price exceeds $250,000
choice_c: Only when representing the buyer, never when representing the seller
choice_d: Only when no attorney is involved anywhere in the transaction
explanation: REEB 16.04(1) states that, except as provided in the exceptions in subs. (2) and (3), a licensee shall use approved forms when acting as an agent or a party in a real estate or business opportunity transaction — this is the core mandate underlying the entire approved-forms system.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(1) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(2), if no board-approved form exists for a particular type of transaction, under what condition may a licensee use a form drafted by a party or an attorney?
choice_a: Only if the name of the drafter is imprinted on the form before it is used by the licensee
choice_b: Only if the licensee first obtains written pre-approval of that specific form from the board
choice_c: The licensee may never use a non-approved form under any circumstances
choice_d: Only if the form is used exclusively for commercial, not residential, transactions
explanation: REEB 16.04(2) permits use of a form drafted by a party or an attorney, when no board-approved form exists for that transaction type, provided the name of the drafter is imprinted on the form before use by the licensee (with a listing firm treated as a party for listing-contract purposes).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(2) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(3), what may a licensee acting as an agent do instead of using an approved contractual form?
choice_a: Negotiate the agreement and permit the parties, or an attorney for one of the parties, to draft or prepare a contractual agreement embodying all the negotiated terms
choice_b: Draft the final contract personally on the firm's own non-approved letterhead template
choice_c: Skip written documentation entirely and rely on an oral agreement between the parties
choice_d: Require the parties to hire the firm's in-house counsel to draft the agreement
explanation: REEB 16.04(3) allows a licensee acting as an agent to negotiate an agreement and let the parties, or an attorney for one of the parties, draft or prepare the final contractual agreement embodying the negotiated terms — an exception to the general approved-forms mandate.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.04(3) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(1), which of the following is a licensee prohibited from doing?
choice_a: Giving advice or an opinion about the legal rights or obligations of parties to a transaction, the legal effect of a specific contract or conveyance, or the state of title to real estate
choice_b: Filling in the blanks on a board-approved offer to purchase at a buyer's instruction
choice_c: Delivering a completed, board-approved listing contract to the seller for signature
choice_d: Explaining, in general terms, what a standard contingency provision in an approved form typically means
explanation: REEB 16.05(1) draws the core unauthorized-practice-of-law line: a licensee may not give advice or an opinion on the legal rights or obligations of the parties, the legal effect of a specific contract or conveyance, or the state of title to real estate. Completing/delivering approved forms and giving general explanations (16.05(2)) remain permitted.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(1) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(2), what limited explanation may a licensee still give despite the general prohibition on legal advice?
choice_a: A general explanation of the provisions in an approved form when completing it or delivering it for acceptance by the parties
choice_b: A binding legal opinion on how a specific contingency clause would be interpreted by a court
choice_c: An opinion on whether the seller holds clear, marketable title to the property
choice_d: Advice on which party would prevail in a hypothetical breach-of-contract lawsuit
explanation: REEB 16.05(2) carves out a narrow exception: notwithstanding the prohibition in 16.05(1), a licensee may give a general explanation of the provisions in an approved form when completing or delivering it for the parties' acceptance — this stops short of legal opinions on rights, contract effect, or title.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(2) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(3) and (4), what two limits apply to a licensee's completion of approved forms even when otherwise permitted?
choice_a: The use of approved forms must be incidental to the licensee's real estate practice, and the licensee may not make a separate charge for completing an approved form
choice_b: The licensee must complete the form only in the physical presence of both parties, and must charge a flat statutory fee for doing so
choice_c: The form must be reviewed by the board before each use, and a $50 filing fee must be paid per form
choice_d: The licensee must be a broker (never a salesperson), and must have at least five years of licensure
explanation: REEB 16.05(3) limits a licensee to using approved forms only when acting as a licensee or as a principal, and only incidentally to real estate practice; REEB 16.05(4) bars any separate charge for completing an approved form in connection with a transaction.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.05(3), (4) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(e), when a firm reproduces a board-approved contractual form, what must it do with the board's approval statement and date?
choice_a: Retain the board's approval statement and date in the upper left corner exactly as they appear on the board-approved form
choice_b: Remove the approval statement and replace it with the firm's own certification
choice_c: Move the approval statement to the last page of the document
choice_d: The approval statement is optional and may be omitted if the firm's logo appears elsewhere on the form
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(e) requires a firm reproducing an approved form to retain the board's approval statement and date in the upper left corner exactly as it appears on the board-approved form, as part of the broader reproduction requirements (identical line numbering, no concealed optional provisions, firm identification added, and substantially identical formatting).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(e) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(3), may a licensee cross out a provision on an approved form to reflect a party's negotiated agreement?
choice_a: Yes, provided the deleted provision remains legible
choice_b: No, crossing out any language on an approved form is prohibited under all circumstances
choice_c: Yes, but only if the crossed-out text is completely obliterated so it cannot be read
choice_d: Yes, but only a supervising broker (never the licensee who prepared the form) may cross out language
explanation: REEB 16.06(3) permits a licensee to cross out provisions on an approved form to reflect a party's agreement, provided the deleted provisions remain legible — the opposite of choice C, which would violate the legibility requirement.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(3) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(6), what may a licensee do with an approved exclusive right to sell listing contract?
choice_a: Alter it to create an exclusive agency listing, an open listing, or a one-party listing
choice_b: Alter it to remove the commission provision entirely without the seller's agreement
choice_c: Convert it into a property management agreement without any additional drafting
choice_d: Extend its term indefinitely without the seller's written consent
explanation: REEB 16.06(6) permits a licensee to alter an approved exclusive right to sell listing contract to create an exclusive agency listing, an open listing, or a one-party listing — recognizing that these related listing types share the same approved-form base.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(6) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(7), which version of a board-approved form must a licensee use?
choice_a: The latest approved version of the board-approved form
choice_b: Whichever version the licensee's firm printed most recently in bulk, even if outdated
choice_c: Any version published within the last ten years
choice_d: The version the client specifically requests, regardless of the board's current version
explanation: REEB 16.06(7) requires a licensee to use the latest approved version of a board-approved form, so continuing to use a superseded version — even one printed in bulk by the firm — is not compliant.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(7) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(4), what condition applies before a licensee may attach a pre-prepared addendum that relates to blanks on, or alters optional provisions within, an approved form?
choice_a: The addendum must be prepared by the firm or by an attorney who is identified on the addendum, and must be incorporated by reference into the properly related approved form
choice_b: The addendum may be prepared by anyone, with no identification required, as long as it is stapled to the approved form
choice_c: The addendum must first be filed with and separately approved by the Real Estate Examining Board before each use
choice_d: The addendum may only be used if it is handwritten by the licensee at the closing table
explanation: REEB 16.06(4) permits a firm- or attorney-prepared addendum (with the attorney identified on it) that relates to an approved form's blanks or alters/supplants its optional provisions, so long as it is incorporated by reference and properly related to the approved form — no case-by-case board pre-approval is required.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(4) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(b), which category of approved forms is identified by specific Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) form numbers, such as UCC forms 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 410, 411, 430, 445, 450, and 451?
choice_a: Uniform Commercial Code forms specifically enumerated by number in the rule
choice_b: State Bar of Wisconsin conveyance forms
choice_c: Property management agreement forms
choice_d: Out-of-state contractual forms
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(b) approves a specific enumerated list of Uniform Commercial Code forms (numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 410, 411, 430, 445, 450, and 451) as approved forms, distinct from the State Bar conveyance forms approved in REEB 16.03(1)(a).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(b) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(d), forms prepared by which entities are recognized as approved forms when used in programs the entity administers under authority provided by law?
choice_a: Governmental, quasi-governmental, and tribal agencies
choice_b: Private title insurance underwriters
choice_c: Local multiple listing services (MLS organizations)
choice_d: Wisconsin-licensed home inspectors
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(d) approves forms prepared by governmental, quasi-governmental, and tribal agencies for use in programs those agencies administer under authority provided by law, such as housing-assistance or first-time homebuyer program documents.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(d) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(2), beyond forms the board itself prepares and approves under § 452.05(1)(b), Stats., which forms does the board additionally approve specifically for use by salespersons, and where are current board-approved forms made available?
choice_a: The forms described in REEB 16.03(1)(c), (d), and (e) are approved for salesperson use, and current board-approved contractual forms are made available on the department's webpage
choice_b: Only broker-level licensees, never salespersons, may use any form described in REEB 16.03(1)(c) through (e), and forms are available only by mailed request
choice_c: All forms in REEB 16.03(1) are automatically restricted to brokers with at least five years of experience
choice_d: Salespersons may use forms under REEB 16.03(1)(c) through (e) only after receiving individualized written board permission for each transaction
explanation: REEB 16.03(2) separately extends board approval of the out-of-state (c), governmental/tribal (d), and property management (e) forms specifically for use by salespersons, and states that board-approved contractual forms for real estate practice are made available on the department's webpage.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(2) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(2), what special restriction applies to forms approved under REEB 16.03(1)(a) or (b) (State Bar of Wisconsin forms and Uniform Commercial Code forms) that goes beyond the general rule for other approved forms?
choice_a: A licensee who reproduces or arranges for printing one of these forms may not modify it in any way
choice_b: These forms may be reproduced only in a font size smaller than the original
choice_c: These forms require a notarized certificate of authenticity attached before every use
choice_d: These forms may only be reproduced by the Real Estate Examining Board itself, never by a firm
explanation: REEB 16.06(2) bars any modification whatsoever to State Bar of Wisconsin forms and UCC forms approved under REEB 16.03(1)(a)-(b) when reproduced — a stricter rule than the general cross-out permission under REEB 16.06(3), which applies to other board-approved contractual forms such as those the board itself drafts.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(2) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(a), what must a firm ensure when it reproduces or arranges for the printing of a board-approved contractual form?
choice_a: That the numbering of lines, the content of each line, and the lines appearing on each page are identical to those on the board-approved form
choice_b: That the reproduced form uses a different line-numbering scheme so it cannot be confused with the original
choice_c: That each page is printed on legal-size paper regardless of the board-approved form's original page size
choice_d: That the firm's logo appears on every line of the form
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(a) requires that the line numbering, line contents, and the lines appearing on each page match the board-approved form exactly whenever a firm reproduces it.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(a) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(b), what is a firm prohibited from doing when reproducing a board-approved form?
choice_a: Reproducing the form so that optional provisions are omitted and blank lines are filled in without any indication of where those optional provisions and blank lines occur on the board-approved form
choice_b: Including any optional provisions at all, even if they remain unmarked and unfilled
choice_c: Printing the form using black ink rather than blue ink
choice_d: Providing the form to a party in electronic form instead of on paper
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(b) bars a firm from reproducing a form in a way that conceals where optional provisions or blank lines occurred on the original board-approved form, preventing licensees from hiding omissions from the parties to a transaction.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(b) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(c), what must a firm indicate on a form it reproduces or arranges to have printed?
choice_a: That the form is reproduced by the firm, stating the firm's address and telephone number at an appropriate place on the form
choice_b: The individual commission percentage the firm intends to charge on the transaction
choice_c: The name of every past client who has previously used that exact form
choice_d: A watermark reading "COPY" across the center of every page
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(c) requires the reproducing firm to identify itself on the form, including its address and telephone number, at an appropriate place on the document.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(c) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(5), what additional restriction applies to a pre-prepared addendum that supplants or alters the printed provisions of an approved form, beyond what REEB 16.06(4) requires for an addendum that merely relates to blanks on the form?
choice_a: The addendum must be drafted by an attorney who is identified on the addendum, and it may contain no optional or multiple-choice provisions and no blank lines other than signature spaces and required identifying items
choice_b: The addendum must be notarized by a Wisconsin notary public before it may be attached to the approved form
choice_c: The addendum must be filed with the Real Estate Examining Board within 10 days after the transaction closes
choice_d: The addendum may be prepared by the licensee personally, with no attorney involvement required
explanation: REEB 16.06(4) allows a firm- or attorney-prepared addendum relating to a form's blanks, but REEB 16.06(5) imposes a stricter standard for an addendum that supplants or alters the form's printed provisions: it must be attorney-drafted (with the attorney identified) and contain no optional or multiple-choice provisions, and no blank lines except for signatures and required identifying items.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(5) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(8), what standard governs how a licensee must use approved forms and prepare addenda?
choice_a: The licensee shall use approved forms and prepare addenda in a manner that adequately accomplishes the contractual instruction of the person for whom the licensee uses the forms and prepares the addenda
choice_b: The licensee must use the shortest possible version of any approved form available for a given transaction type
choice_c: The licensee must obtain a second licensee's countersignature on every addendum before it is attached
choice_d: The licensee must limit addenda to no more than one page regardless of the transaction's complexity
explanation: REEB 16.06(8) sets a functional adequacy standard: a licensee's use of approved forms and preparation of addenda must adequately accomplish the contractual instruction of the person for whom the licensee is completing them.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(8) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(9), an approved buyer agency/tenant representation agreement may be altered by a licensee to create which other types of agreements?
choice_a: An exclusive right to negotiate, exclusive right to locate, or exclusive right to locate and negotiate buyer agency/tenant representation agreement
choice_b: A property management agreement between the firm and a landlord
choice_c: An open listing agreement for the sale of the buyer's current home
choice_d: A deed transferring the buyer's interest in the property to the firm
explanation: REEB 16.06(9) permits a licensee to alter an approved buyer agency/tenant representation agreement to create an exclusive right to negotiate, exclusive right to locate, or exclusive right to locate and negotiate version — paralleling the listing-contract alteration rule in REEB 16.06(6).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(9) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.40(2), which activity is expressly identified as NOT constituting prohibited legal advice by a licensee?
choice_a: A supervising broker's review of transaction documents conducted under § 452.132(4), Stats.
choice_b: A licensee's opinion on whether a title defect is legally curable
choice_c: A licensee's interpretation of a specific indemnification clause for one of the parties
choice_d: A licensee's prediction of how a court would likely rule on a boundary dispute
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.40(2) clarifies that a supervising broker's document review under § 452.132(4), Stats. — which checks for board-approved-form compliance and errors apparent on the face of a document — is not treated as prohibited legal advice, distinguishing it from the substantive legal opinions the statute otherwise bars.
source_note: Wis. Stat. § 452.40(2), cross-referencing § 452.132(4), Stats. (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(2e), (2m), and (2s), how does an "exclusive right to locate and negotiate" buyer agency/tenant representation agreement differ from an "exclusive right to locate" agreement and an "exclusive right to negotiate" agreement?
choice_a: The locate-and-negotiate version gives the firm the exclusive right to both find an interest in property AND negotiate its procurement for the client, while the other two agreements grant only one of those two exclusive rights alone
choice_b: The locate-and-negotiate version has no minimum term, while the other two must run for exactly six months
choice_c: The locate-and-negotiate version may be used only for commercial tenant representation, never for buyers of residential property
choice_d: There is no substantive difference; the three terms are interchangeable under REEB 16.02
explanation: REEB 16.02(2e) defines the exclusive-right-to-locate agreement as covering only the firm's exclusive right to find an interest in property, REEB 16.02(2s) defines the exclusive-right-to-negotiate agreement as covering only the exclusive right to negotiate procurement, and REEB 16.02(2m) defines the exclusive-right-to-locate-and-negotiate agreement as combining both rights.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(2e), (2m), (2s) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(3m), a "listing contract" is best described as which of the following?
choice_a: A written agency agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services to a client for the sale or rental of property, under terms by which the firm may earn a commission
choice_b: Any written agreement between two licensees to split a commission on a co-listed property
choice_c: A written agreement authorizing a firm to locate, but not negotiate, an interest in property on behalf of a buyer
choice_d: An oral understanding between an owner and a firm that is reduced to writing only after a buyer is found
explanation: REEB 16.02(3m) defines "listing contract" as a written agency agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services for the sale or rental of property, with terms for earning a commission. Choice C instead describes a buyer agency/tenant representation concept under REEB 16.02(1m)/(2e), and choice D conflicts with the written-agreement requirement.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(3m) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.01, what statutory provisions are cited as authority for the rules in chapter REEB 16?
choice_c: Wis. Stat. §§ 452.09 and 452.10 only
choice_d: Wis. Stat. § 452.40 only, since it is the parallel statute on forms and legal advice
explanation: REEB 16.01 states that the rules in chapter REEB 16 are adopted pursuant to ss. 227.11(2) (general agency rulemaking authority), 452.05(1)(b) (board's authority to prepare and approve forms), 452.07, and 452.14(3)(m), Stats. — the same disciplinary cross-reference later invoked by REEB 16.07.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.01 (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1), how is the term "agency agreement" defined for purposes of chapter REEB 16?
choice_a: It has the meaning given in Wis. Stat. § 452.01(1m): a written agreement between a firm and a client in which the client authorizes the firm to provide brokerage services to the client
choice_b: It is independently defined within REEB 16.02(1) itself, without reference to any statute
choice_c: It has the meaning given in Wis. Stat. § 452.135(1), the agency-disclosure-to-customers statute
choice_d: It means any oral understanding between a firm and a client regarding brokerage services
explanation: REEB 16.02(1) does not restate the definition but instead incorporates it by cross-reference: "agency agreement" has the meaning given in Wis. Stat. § 452.01(1m), which defines it as a written agreement between a firm and a client authorizing the firm to provide brokerage services to the client.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1), cross-referencing Wis. Stat. § 452.01(1m) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1m), what is a "buyer agency/tenant representation agreement" — the base agreement that the exclusive-right-to-locate, -negotiate, and -locate-and-negotiate versions in REEB 16.02(2e), (2m), and (2s) each alter?
choice_a: A written agency agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services to the client for the procurement of an interest in property, and providing the terms whereby the firm may earn a commission
choice_b: A written agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services to a client for the sale or rental of the client's own property
choice_c: An oral agreement authorizing a firm to search for available rental units on a tenant's behalf, with no commission terms required
choice_d: A written agreement between two firms allocating a commission on a co-represented transaction
explanation: REEB 16.02(1m) defines "buyer agency/tenant representation agreement" as a written agency agreement authorizing a firm to provide brokerage services for the procurement of an interest in property, with terms for earning a commission — the buyer/tenant-side counterpart to the "listing contract" defined in REEB 16.02(3m) for the seller/landlord side.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.02(1m) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(d), besides preserving the board-approved form's line numbering and content, what else is a firm prohibited from doing when it reproduces the form?
choice_a: Adding additional blank lines, adding additional lines containing textual content, or otherwise altering the form's format in any other manner
choice_b: Printing the reproduced form on colored paper instead of white paper
choice_c: Distributing the reproduced form to more than one party in the transaction
choice_d: Charging the firm's standard letterhead-printing fee for the reproduction
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(d) bars a firm from adding additional blank lines or lines of textual content, or altering the format of a reproduced board-approved form in any other manner — reinforcing the identical-formatting mandate in REEB 16.06(1)(a) and (f).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(d) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(f), what must a firm assure about the formatting of a form it reproduces or arranges to have printed?
choice_a: That the formatting of the reproduced form is substantially identical to that on the board-approved form
choice_b: That the formatting is simplified and condensed compared to the board-approved form
choice_c: That the formatting matches the firm's standard branded template rather than the board-approved form
choice_d: That the formatting need only substantially match other firms' versions of the same form, not the board-approved original
explanation: REEB 16.06(1)(f) is the catch-all formatting requirement: a firm reproducing a board-approved form must assure the formatting is substantially identical to the board-approved form, in addition to the specific line-numbering, content, and no-added-lines requirements of REEB 16.06(1)(a) and (d).
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.06(1)(f) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Stat. § 452.40(1)(b), who is authorized to use a form approved by the board under § 452.05(1)(b), Stats., in real estate practice?
choice_a: A firm and any licensee associated with the firm
choice_b: Only a supervising broker, never an associated salesperson
choice_c: Only a party to the transaction who is not represented by a licensee
choice_d: Only an attorney retained by one of the parties to the transaction
explanation: Wis. Stat. § 452.40(1)(b) authorizes a firm and any licensee associated with the firm to use a board-approved form in real estate practice — the statutory-level counterpart to the approved-forms mandate implemented in detail by REEB chapter 16.
source_note: Wis. Stat. § 452.40(1)(b) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)

question: Under Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(e), an approved property management agreement's provisions must relate to which four subject areas concerning the landlord's property?
choice_a: Leasing, managing, marketing, and overall management of the property
choice_b: Financing, insuring, appraising, and taxing the property
choice_c: Listing, advertising, showing, and closing the sale of the property
choice_d: Inspecting, repairing, permitting, and zoning the property
explanation: REEB 16.03(1)(e) approves property management agreement forms whose provisions relate to leasing, managing, marketing, and overall management of the landlord's property, when prepared by the broker entering into the agreement, an attorney, or the landlord.
source_note: Wis. Admin. Code § REEB 16.03(1)(e) (live-verified at docs.legis.wisconsin.gov)
